title: adaptive_sf_select does not clamp assigned_sf/return to [7,12] (latent, pre-existing)
description: Found by security codereview of worker6-b7z9.30.3 (density threshold 8 + floors). Rust RfHealthMetrics::adaptive_sf_select (rust/lichen-core/src/rf_health.rs ~:414) takes assigned_sf: Option<u8> unvalidated and returns it unclamped: adaptive_sf_select(Some(0), None, None) -> (0, true); Some(200) -> (200, true); Some(6) -> 6. The new floors only raise under bad RF; they do not bound the returned SF. Currently latent: the only callers are tests feeding schema-valid 7-12 values. But spec 2a.8/02-physical-link define ASSIGNED_SF as a DIO-signaled 1-byte field — when a future caller wires DIO signaling into this function, attacker-influenced bytes will reach radio configuration directly. Fix: clamp sf to [7,12] (SF_MIN/SF_MAX per spec 2a.8:636) at entry or before return, or validate assigned_sf and reject out-of-range. Also mirror in the C gradient.c sf_select if it has the same shape. Pre-existing (not introduced by b7z9.30.3, whose floors only mask it under bad-RF conditions).
close_reason: Clamped assigned_sf to [7,12] (SF_MIN/SF_MAX per spec 2a.8:636) at adaptive_sf_select entry (rf_health.rs:648-651), matching python ccp.py:346 max(7,min(12,sf)) parity — the C gradient.c sf_select already bounds out-of-range stored SF to default (gradient.c:319-321), so C needed no change. New test adaptive_sf_select_clamps_assigned_sf_to_spec_range covers 0/6->7, 200/13->12 with tx_allowed asserted on the neutral baseline (verified genuinely neutral: all gates disengage). Verification: 412 lichen-core lib tests pass incl. the new test; all 24 assigned_sf values across ccp15/ccp16 vector JSONs are in [7,12] so the committed oracle corpus is conformance-neutral to the clamp. 3x codereview delegated to kimi-k3 (correctness/security/robustness): all PASS with zero defects; nits only. Findings filed, not fixed inline: project-LICHEN-worker6-kvfd (P2, pre-existing ccp16_desync_vectors.rs+yggdrasil_addr_vectors.rs missing serde_json::Value import blocks the whole crate test target) and a P4 for the stale util_fp_scale doc reference at rf_health.rs:633.
